thread:
anya: Quick sync — need final decision on: (1) short statuspage copy for last week's API outage, (2) whether RCA is public or available on request, and (3) redaction rules for customer-facing RCA. Goal: finalize by EOD Thu so support can send follow-ups.

olivia: can you paste the current draft statuspage blurb? i have small edits.

anya: sure — draft below:
```
Status: Incident resolved
Summary: We experienced elevated API error rates between 2026-03-18 02:10 UTC and 2026-03-18 03:45 UTC due to a degraded autoscaling path that prevented new worker allocations. Impact: a subset of request types returned 500 errors or timed out. Mitigation: we rolled forward a fix and resumed normal autoscaling. Customers may see elevated latency for a short window after the rollback while caches warmed.
Next steps: a full post-incident summary and remediation timeline will be provided.
```

olivia: I suggest tightening language around impact. "a subset of request types" is vague — say "requests with large payloads or client-side streaming"? Also change "rolled forward a fix" to "deployed a targeted config rollback".

mike: +1 on tightening. We should also avoid internal terms like "autoscaling path" on the public page. Replace with "capacity provisioning".

sam: for customer comms, we need a short sentence telling customers how to get more details: prefer "RCA available on request for affected customers" vs "public RCA". Legal has pushed us toward on-request for anything that includes traces.

nina: legal note — we can publish high-level RCA but must redact any customer-identifying logs. On-request RCAs should require an NDA or redaction checklist signed by CS.

olivia: proposed final statuspage blurb (short):
```
Status: Resolved
Summary: Between 02:10–03:45 UTC on 2026-03-18, certain API requests experienced increased errors due to a capacity provisioning failure. We deployed a targeted configuration rollback; services have returned to normal. Affected customers may request a detailed incident summary from support.
```

anya: that reads well. agree to "request a detailed incident summary" rather than 'RCA' in the public page.

mike: decision on making the RCA public? my take: don't publish full RCA. Provide a redacted public summary (what olivia posted) and share a fuller RCA on request with redaction performed by infra + legal. Owner: mike to coordinate redaction and sign-off. Timeline: draft redaction done by Fri EOD, final sign-off Mon.

sam: support process: when a customer requests the detailed summary, CS will open a ticket to infra-redaction queue. Need template for what we include. I'll draft template by Thu.

nina: redaction checklist highlights: remove customer IDs, remove raw traces with IPs, mask S3 keys and internal hostnames. Also annotate any retained metrics with sampling details.

anya: also flagged recurring pattern: this is the third scaling-related incident in 9 months. we should add a recurring-incident action item in the postmortem tracker: root cause deeper look + runbook updates + additional e2e load tests.

mike: tracking — I'll open the remediation epic and link it in the postmortem. ownership: infra-runtime team. timeline: initial mitigation proposals by Apr 8.

olivia: Action items summary (I'll own the statuspage copy):
1) Finalize public statuspage copy — owner: olivia — due: Thu EOD
2) Draft CS template for on-request incident summaries — owner: sam — due: Thu EOD
3) Redaction draft for RCA + legal sign-off — owner: mike + nina — draft due: Fri EOD, sign-off Mon
4) Open remediation epic for recurring scaling incidents — owner: mike — create by Mon, proposals by Apr 8

anya: scheduling check — propose 30m sync Fri 10am to confirm redaction progress and CS template. who can join?

mike: I can. olivia?

olivia: yes.

sam: yes.

incident-bot: Incident 2026-03-18-API-123 closed by anya. Postmortem created: https://redwood.company/postmortems/2026-03-18-API-123

anya: thanks everyone. please add any missing owners here. if no objections I'll publish the statuspage update with olivia's copy after legal confirms the redaction approach.

mike: no objections from infra.

nina: legal tbd — i will review redaction checklist by Thu morning.

anya: perfect — closing thread. :thumbsup:
